outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the family has moved in several places: Ma (25 Aug 2026) gives counterexamples to the Peskine–Szpiro dimension inequality, grade conjecture and strong intersection conjecture; Böhmler–Marczinzik (10 Aug 2026) disprove a Huneke–Şega–Vraciu Tor-vanishing conjecture; Pham (Aug–Sep 2026) and Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar (Aug 2026) give counterexamples to the Huneke–Wiegand conjecture in its general Gorenstein form; AI-assisted counterexamples to Auslander–Reiten and Tachikawa-type conjectures for Artin algebras were reported in Sep–Oct 2026; and within the Wikipedia article's own named list, Serre's positivity conjecture gained only a partial result (Serre-liftable modules, April 2024) while the direct summand conjecture and the new intersection theorem were settled before the window.
problem_asks: The bullet names a family, not one question: the homological conjectures of commutative algebra. Its link is the Wikipedia article 'Homological conjectures in commutative algebra', whose named list (as fetched) asks, part by part: (1) Zero Divisor Theorem: if a nonzero module M of finite projective dimension has r a nonzerodivisor on M, is r a nonzerodivisor on R? (2) Bass's Question: does a nonzero module with finite injective resolution force R Cohen–Macaulay? (3) Intersection Theorem: if M⊗N is nonzero of finite length, is dim N ≤ pd M? (4) New Intersection Theorem: for a finite complex of free modules with nonzero finite-length total homology, dim R ≤ n? (5) Improved New Intersection Conjecture: same set-up with H₀ having a minimal generator killed by a power of the maximal ideal; conclusion dim R ≤ n. (6) Direct Summand Conjecture: R regular and R ⊆ S module-finite implies R is a direct summand of S. (7) Canonical Element Conjecture. (8) Existence of balanced big Cohen–Macaulay modules. (9) Cohen–Macaulayness of direct summands of regular rings. (10) Vanishing conjecture for maps of Tor. (11) Strong Direct Summand Conjecture. (12) Existence of weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras. (13) Serre's conjecture on multiplicities: vanishing and positivity of intersection multiplicities for regular R (the article states Serre proved the sum cannot exceed d). (14) Small Cohen–Macaulay modules conjecture: a complete local ring has a nonzero finitely generated module on which some, equivalently every, system of parameters is regular. The linked article names none of the following, though they belong to the same literature and may fall under the family: Peskine–Szpiro dimension, grade and strong intersection conjectures; the Huneke–Şega–Vraciu Tor-vanishing conjecture; the Huneke–Wiegand conjecture; and the Auslander–Reiten, Nakayama and Tachikawa conjectures (commutative and Artin-algebra forms). Whether those are in the bullet's scope is for the later pass; each is recorded below as its own event.

events.what_happened: Peskine and Szpiro, 'Dimension projective finie et cohomologie locale', Publ. Math. IHÉS 42 (1973). Proves the Intersection Theorem (item 3) and, in characteristic p, the New Intersection Theorem (item 4). Cited as [PS73] in Ma's preprint (2608.24018) and by a search snippet of the IHÉS title; the 1973 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Intersection Theorem for Noetherian local rings: for nonzero finitely generated M, N with M⊗N of finite length and M of finite projective dimension, dim N ≤ pd M. New Intersection Theorem in characteristic p>0. Consequences, per secondary sources: Auslander's zero-divisor theorem and Bass's question (items 1–2).
events.remains: Items 5–14 of the named list were open at this point and are addressed by other events. The Peskine–Szpiro dimension inequality (dim M + dim N ≤ dim R) is not what this theorem gives; it is the separate question that the 2026 counterexamples concern.
events.direction: Proves the intersection-theorem inequality dim N ≤ pd M; consistent with the list's item 3 being true.

events.what_happened: Hochster extends the New Intersection Theorem to all equicharacteristic local rings by reduction to characteristic p (announced in the AMS Bulletin 1974; full work 1975, per secondary accounts). The exact year varies between 1973/74 and 1975 depending on whether the announcement or the paper is counted. Supported only by search snippets; not opened.
events.delivers: New Intersection Theorem (item 4) for all equicharacteristic local rings.
events.remains: Mixed characteristic New Intersection Theorem (see Roberts 1987); improved version (item 5) not settled by this event.
events.doubts: Year uncertain (1973/74/75) and the source is a search snippet; not verified.
events.direction: Confirms item 4 in equal characteristic.

Proves Serre's positivity conjecture for Serre liftable modules over ramified regular local rings, and a lower bound on the length of nonzero Serre liftable modules by Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity (special cases of the Length Conjecture of Iyengar, Ma and Walker).

Extends, for cML rings, the Peskine–Szpiro relation between cohomological dimension and height of a Cohen–Macaulay ideal.

events.what_happened: Ma, 'Local cohomological dimension and depth in mixed characteristic', arXiv:2608.08092 (v1 8 Aug 2026). In an unramified regular local ring of mixed characteristic: depth(R/I) ≥ 3 implies cd(I) ≤ d−3; for R essentially of finite type over a DVR, depth(R/I) ≥ 4 implies cd(I) ≤ d−4; local cohomology H^j_I(R) is a Q-vector space for j > d − depth(R/I).
events.delivers: Cohomological-dimension bounds in mixed characteristic. Does not name the Peskine–Szpiro dimension inequality or the homological conjectures per the abstract.
events.remains: The Peskine–Szpiro dimension inequality and grade/strong intersection conjectures.
events.direction: Does not cut against any named conjecture per its abstract; neighbour only.

events.what_happened: Ma, 'Counterexamples to Peskine–Szpiro's conjecture on modules of finite projective dimension', arXiv:2608.24018 (v1 25 Aug 2026; only version seen). Gives counterexamples to the remaining homological conjectures of Peskine and Szpiro (PS73) for modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings: the dimension inequality, the strong intersection conjecture, and the grade conjecture are each false in general. Conjecture 1 in the paper states: for M f.g. of finite pd and N f.g. with M⊗N of finite length, (i) dim M + dim N ≤ dim R; (ii) dim N ≤ grade M (the strong intersection conjecture); (iii) grade M = dim R − dim M (the grade conjecture). The paper says (ii) is equivalent to (i) together with (iii), citing PS II Théorème (0.10).
events.revisions: v1 only (arXiv abstract page, 25 Aug 2026 03:18 UTC).
events.delivers: (a) Dimension inequality (i) fails for some Noetherian complete local ring of dimension 3 (ring R = k[[x,y,z,w,u]]/(xw−yz, ux, uz) per the paper's §2.3 as summarised; the stated theorem is 'a Noetherian complete local ring of dimension three for which the dimension inequality does not hold'). (b) Grade conjecture (iii) fails for some complete local ring of dimension 4 (R′ = k[[x,y,z,w,u,v]]/(xw−yz, ux, uz, vx, vz) with M′ of finite pd, dim 1, grade M′ ≤ 2 ≠ 3, per §2.4 as summarised). (c) Strong intersection conjecture (ii) fails in general, as a consequence of (a) and (b) with the paper's equivalence. Restrictions: the counterexamples are complete local rings of dimension 3 and 4; the paper says 'false in general' and does not, in the abstract, say which subclasses keep the statements.
events.remains: Which subclasses of Noetherian local rings (regular, depth ≤1, equicharacteristic, excellent, Gorenstein, others) keep the dimension inequality, grade conjecture or strong intersection conjecture is not settled by this event. Serre's regular-ring case of (i) and the depth ≤1 case (see the Christensen–Nasseh event) are not touched.

checked_by.who: Lars Winther Christensen and Saeed Nasseh
checked_by.qualification: Active commutative and homological algebraists, authors of arXiv:2610.03871 on the same inequality. I did not verify their affiliations or publication records.
checked_by.what_they_did: Cite §2.3 of Ma's preprint and say: 'An example by Ma [4, §2.3] shows that the Dimension Inequality does not hold in general.' They do not check the construction in their note.

events.doubts: No specific error identified in any source I read. Not checked by me: the construction itself. I read the abstract, the introduction's Conjecture 1 and AI-disclosure paragraph, and a summary of §2.3 and §2.4 from a fetch tool; the PDF text was not readable. Christensen–Nasseh's note renders Ma's dimensions as '33' and '22' where the search summary and the preprint text say '3' and '2', which I take to be a rendering artefact but have not confirmed.
events.direction: Cuts against the general dimension inequality (dim M + dim N ≤ dim R), the grade conjecture and the strong intersection conjecture, as the problem's Peskine–Szpiro family is stated in Conjecture 1.
events.object: Explicit commutative complete local rings. (a) R = k[[x,y,z,w,u]]/(xw−yz, ux, uz), dimension 3, with a finitely generated module M of finite projective dimension and dim M = 1, and a module B (built from C[[u]], C = A/P) such that M⊗B has finite length and dim M + dim B = 1 + 3 > 3 = dim R. The module M = H⁰ of a perfect complex obtained by Milnor patching over a fibre product A ×_C B; the construction is an explicit gluing argument, not an existence proof. (b) R′ = k[[x,y,z,w,u,v]]/(xw−yz, ux, uz, vx, vz), dimension 4, with M′ of finite projective dimension, dimension 1 and grade M′ ≤ 2 ≠ 3 = dim R′ − dim M′. Both build on the Dutta–Hochster–McLaughlin example of negative intersection multiplicity (Invent. Math. 1985). Whether these contradict the statement of the problem is for the later pass.

events.what_happened: Christensen and Nasseh, 'Peskine and Szpiro’s Dimension Inequality holds over local rings of depth at most one', arXiv:2610.03871 (v1 2 Oct 2026, 4 pp.). Proves that the general version of the Peskine–Szpiro Dimension Inequality (the version including the dimension of the tensor product) holds over Noetherian local rings of depth at most one. The note cites Ma's §2.3 counterexample as showing the inequality fails in general.
events.delivers: Dimension inequality dim M + dim N ≤ dim R (general form, with dimension of the tensor product) for Noetherian local rings of depth ≤ 1. Restriction: depth ≤ 1 only.
events.remains: The dimension inequality for local rings of depth ≥ 2 (where Ma's counterexample lives) and the grade and strong intersection conjectures.
events.direction: Confirms the dimension inequality on a restricted class; consistent with Ma's counterexample living outside it.

events.what_happened: Böhmler and Marczinzik, 'Tor and Ext vanishing results for commutative Artinian rings', arXiv:2608.09701 (v1 10 Aug 2026; only version). Theorem 0.3: for R = K[x,y]/(xy, x²−y³) (five-dimensional over K), M = R/(y), N = R/(x−y), one has m²M = 0 and m²N = 0, Tor_i^R(M,N) = 0 for all i ≥ 1, but m³ ≠ 0. This disproves the Huneke–Şega–Vraciu conjecture that these hypotheses force m³ = 0.
events.delivers: Counterexample to the Huneke–Şega–Vraciu Tor-vanishing conjecture over commutative finite-dimensional local algebras (as stated: m²M = m²N = 0 and Tor vanishing ⇒ m³ = 0). Restricted to the conjecture's own statement; does not rule out other bounds on m^k.
events.remains: Whether a corrected bound holds, and whether Tor vanishing with m²-annihilated modules forces other conclusions, are not addressed by this event.

events.what_happened: Same paper as bm-2026-hsv-tor-vanishing-counterexample (arXiv:2608.09701): negative answer to a question of Avramov, Buchweitz and Şega by constructing a commutative local finite-dimensional non-Gorenstein algebra R (over the rationals) with Ext¹_R(D(R), R) = 0. The Avramov–Buchweitz–Şega conjecture asks for all degrees; the question answered is, as far as I can tell, whether a single degree suffices (the exact wording of the question was not found).

events.what_happened: The manuscript 'A Complete Local Domain without a Small Cohen–Macaulay Module' (OpenAI, dated 23 September 2026) claims a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain R containing ℂ, with residue field ℂ, that has no nonzero finitely generated module of depth 3 (equal to dim R), i.e. no small (maximal) Cohen–Macaulay module. This is the domain form of the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture, which is item (14) of the list's named homological conjectures. The ring is R(X,H), the completion at its homogeneous maximal ideal of T(X,H) = ⊕ H⁰(X, jH), for a smooth projective complex surface X with an ample globally generated H. The specific pair used has n = 7: X is an abelian (ℤ/7)⁵ Kummer cover of the blow-up of ℙ² at four points, branched along the six lines joining them and the four exceptional curves, with H² = 1715. Non-existence is derived from a numerical obstruction (Theorem 1.2 in the manuscript): if R(X,H) admits a small Cohen–Macaulay module then K_X² − 2c₂(X) ≤ 6H², which the chosen surface violates (13377 > 10290). The manuscript also claims a corollary that the uncompleted localisation T_𝔫 is a three-dimensional local domain essentially of finite type over ℂ with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module.
events.delivers: If the claim holds, it refutes the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture in the list's form. The list asks for a nonzero finitely generated module on which some (equivalently every) system of parameters is regular, for every complete local ring. The ring here is a complete local ring with no such module, so the counterexample refutes the list's form. The manuscript itself states only the domain form ('every complete Noetherian local domain has one'), which is a special case of the list's statement, so the two statements do not match word for word; the implication to the list's form is not stated in the text. Restrictions: the counterexample is a normal domain of dimension three in equal characteristic zero (it contains ℂ with residue field ℂ). The non-existence is only for finitely generated modules; the manuscript says big Cohen–Macaulay modules exist and are not affected. The proof uses only the n = 7 member of the surface family. The corollary gives a counterexample in the class of three-dimensional local domains essentially of finite type over ℂ.
events.remains: If the claim is correct, item (14) is settled negatively and nothing in it remains open. Items (1)–(13) of the list's named conjectures (Zero Divisor, Bass's question, Intersection, New Intersection, Improved New Intersection, Direct Summand, Canonical Element, balanced big Cohen–Macaulay existence, Cohen–Macaulayness of direct summands of regular rings, Tor vanishing, Strong Direct Summand, weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras, and Serre's multiplicity conjecture) are not addressed by this manuscript, which cites several of them as already known. The Peskine–Szpiro, Huneke–Şega–Vraciu, Huneke–Wiegand, and Auslander–Reiten/Nakayama/Tachikawa conjectures are not discussed in the text.

disputes.summary: 'Strong intersection conjecture' names two different statements. Ma's preprint (Conjecture 1 (ii)) says dim N ≤ grade M for f.g. M of finite pd with M⊗N of finite length, a Peskine–Szpiro statement that Ma says is false. A secondary lecture-note account (SLMath workshop notes, via search) states a different version, for complexes of free modules over a local ring, and says Dutta showed that version equivalent to the canonical element conjecture and hence to the direct summand conjecture, which is now known. These cannot both be the 'strong intersection conjecture' in the same sense. The Dutta equivalence was not checked in Dutta's own paper (only its abstract, which mentions the improved NIT, was seen).

Auslander–Reiten/Tachikawa equivalence paper (Enomoto–Marczinzik): the authors' own statement says 'ChatGPT Astra was used in author-directed research and manuscript preparation' (developing auxiliary arguments, expanding proof details, literature searches, consistency checks, LaTeX). A MathWorld page credits 'GPT-6 Astra with finding and drafting the proof, with Claude assisting in revision', and a GitHub catalogue of AI results lists the role as 'discovered'. The authors' account governs under the record's rule; the other two are secondary and conflict with each other.

Ma's preprint attributes the dimension-inequality counterexample to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, but attributes the grade-conjecture counterexample to the author ('the author then observed that a minimal modification ... also immediately yields a counterexample to the grade conjecture'). The strong intersection conjecture follows from the two (per the paper's equivalence), so its AI attribution is split.

Huneke–Wiegand: Pham's repository calls its candidate an 'unreviewed candidate, not an established theorem and not a priority claim' with external review pending, while the arXiv paper 2609.07615 is titled as a counterexample and says Huneke independently verified the example (his note not read). Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar state that the conjecture is contradicted, and they cite Pham's request as an 'ai-assisted candidate counterexample'.

Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar's abstract both says a one-dimensional Gorenstein example 'contradicts a conjecture of C. Huneke and R. Wiegand' and that 'a proof of the conjecture ... is presented when the ring is equicharacteristic and its embedding dimension is at most three'. This is consistent only if the counterexample lies outside equicharacteristic embedding-dimension-≤3 rings, which the parts I read do not state.
Name variant: Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar's acknowledgement spells the author 'Song Pham', while the introduction and reference list say 'Son Pham'. The repository and arXiv paper use 'Son Pham'.
Lyle's arXiv:2610.00022 prints 'Submitted on 1 Sep 2026' against an identifier from October 2026 numbering. The date is unresolved.

Christensen–Nasseh's note renders Ma's rings as 'dimension 33' and 'dimension 22'; Ma's preprint, as summarised, gives dimension 3 and a base of dimension 2. The note's rendering is probably an artefact of the text extraction; not confirmed against the PDF.

Mixed-characteristic direct summand conjecture: Bhatt's arXiv v1 (31 Aug 2016) and André's arXiv v1 (1 Sep 2016) are one day apart. Bhatt's abstract claims 'a quicker proof of Hochster's conjecture'; André's abstract says he proposes 'a proof in the framework of P. Scholze's perfectoid theory'. The record does not decide ordering or credit; it records both dates.

Ma's disclosure paragraph says the AI 'found' the dimension counterexample, while Ma's own abstract and Christensen–Nasseh's note treat the counterexamples as the author's. The AI role is the author's own account; it is recorded as load-bearing by that account, and the judging pass should weigh it.

summary: The bullet is a family title, and the frozen Wikipedia article it links (fetched 12 Oct 2026) lists fourteen named Hochster-style items. On that list, the picture before the window is clear: the Intersection Theorem (Peskine–Szpiro 1973), the New Intersection Theorem in all characteristics (1973/75 equichar; Roberts 1987 mixed), the vanishing part of Serre's multiplicity conjecture (Roberts 1985; Gillet–Soulé), the canonical element conjecture in special cases (Dutta 1987), the direct summand conjecture (Heitmann 2002 in dimension three; Bhatt 31 Aug 2016; André 1 Sep 2016 in mixed characteristic), the mixed-characteristic vanishing conjecture for maps of Tor (Heitmann–Ma 2017) and the big Cohen–Macaulay algebras (Hochster–Huneke 1992; André 2016) were all settled before 2024. Inside the window, on the list itself, only one item moved: Serre's positivity conjecture gained a partial result for Serre liftable modules over ramified regular local rings (KC & Soto Levins, v1 26 Apr 2024), and I found nothing in 2024–2026 on the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture, the strong direct summand or improved new intersection conjectures, or the rigidity conjecture. Outside the named list but in the same literature, five developments since 2024 are substantive. (1) Ma (25 Aug 2026) disproves the general Peskine–Szpiro dimension inequality (dim M + dim N ≤ dim R), grade conjecture and Peskine–Szpiro's strong intersection conjecture (dim N ≤ grade M) for Noetherian local rings, using complete local rings of dimensions 3 and 4; his disclosure credits OpenAI’s ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro with discovering the dimension counterexample's construction. Christensen and Nasseh (2 Oct 2026) prove the general inequality over rings of depth ≤ 1 and explicitly say Ma's §2.3 shows it fails in general, so this is an engagement by qualified authors, though not a verification. (2) Böhmler and Marczinzik (10 Aug 2026) disprove the Huneke–Şega–Vraciu conjecture (Tor vanishing with m²-annihilated modules forces m³ = 0) by a five-dimensional algebra, with ChatGPT credited for the example. Their other two results (a negative answer to a question of Avramov–Buchweitz–Şega about Ext¹ alone, and an F₂ example answering a question of Dao) do not refute the Tachikawa-type conjectures as stated. (3) Huneke–Wiegand: Pham's numerical-semigroup candidate (repository undated, cited by 21 Aug 2026; arXiv 2609.07615 on 7 Sep 2026) gives an ideal I = (t^56, t^70) in a one-dimensional Gorenstein domain of characteristic zero with torsion-free I⊗Hom(I,R), which the paper says refutes the Gorenstein formulation; Huneke says he verified it (his note not read); the repository still calls it an unreviewed candidate. Christensen, Gerko and Iyengar (August 2026) give a second counterexample via a field-extension construction, credited to Codex and ChatGPT, and also claim a Codex-found proof for equicharacteristic embedding dimension ≤ 3; those two claims are only consistent if the counterexample sits outside that class, which the parts I read do not say. (4) Artin algebras: Enomoto–Marczinzik (14 Sep 2026; v2 24 Sep) prove the Auslander–Reiten, Nakayama, generalised Nakayama and both Tachikawa conjectures globally equivalent over any fixed commutative artinian base, crediting ChatGPT Astra with auxiliary arguments and proof details; OpenAI's 'Result No. 199' (Lean scope note; secondary date 23 Sep 2026) claims counterexamples to the Auslander–Reiten and second Tachikawa conjectures over an F₂(q,H₁,H₂)-algebra, and a single-author note (7 Oct 2026) extends them to ten homological conjectures, using GPT-6-Astra-Pro and GPT-6-Astra as adversarial reviewers. I could not locate the OpenAI preprints, I did not open the Lean files, and nothing I opened says whether these algebras are commutative. The Artin-algebra results are therefore only within this bullet's scope if the later pass takes the Auslander–Reiten and Tachikawa conjectures as part of 'homological conjectures in commutative algebra', and the commutativity question is decisive for the commutative family. The Peskine–Szpiro items, the Böhmler–Marczinzik items and the Huneke–Wiegand items are commutative and are the clearest candidates for the family. The 'strong intersection conjecture' name collision (Ma's version versus the complexes-of-free-modules version that Dutta relates to the direct summand conjecture) is recorded as a dispute and not resolved here. The AI picture: Ma (ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro; construction credited by the author's own disclosure), Böhmler–Marczinzik (ChatGPT; the example), Pham (GPT-5.6 Pro; the search and example), Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar (Codex and ChatGPT; construction and proof), Enomoto–Marczinzik (ChatGPT Astra; auxiliary arguments), Enomoto's periodicity counterexample (GPT-6-Astra; a different conjecture) and the Hexagon note (GPT-6-Astra(-Pro) as referee; the role in the counterexamples unclear). The OpenAI release names no system in anything I opened. Nothing in 2026 was found from Quanta, Tao's blog or MathOverflow about these results; the one Tao item found concerns the Jacobian conjecture and is out of family.
competing_reading: Strict scope: the bullet's family is the named Hochster list on the frozen article, and on that list nothing moved after January 2024 except Serre's positivity conjecture for a restricted class. Under that reading, the 2026 counterexamples to Peskine–Szpiro, Huneke–Şega–Vraciu, Huneke–Wiegand and the Artin-algebra conjectures are neighbouring problems, and the count is 'nothing happened' with the Serre partial result. Broad scope: the title covers every homological conjecture of commutative algebra, so the Peskine–Szpiro dimension, grade and strong intersection conjectures (Ma), the Huneke–Şega–Vraciu conjecture (Böhmler–Marczinzik) and the Huneke–Wiegand conjecture (Pham; Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar) are falsified in part, with AI credited by the authors for each. Under that reading, the Artin-algebra items fall in or out depending on whether the Auslander–Reiten and Tachikawa conjectures count as commutative-algebra problems. A middle reading accepts the commutative items and leaves the Artin-algebra items as neighbours unless the OpenAI algebras are shown to be commutative.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Scope: whether the bullet's family includes the Peskine–Szpiro, Huneke–Şega–Vraciu, Huneke–Wiegand, Auslander–Reiten, Nakayama and Tachikawa conjectures, which the linked article does not name. (b) Ma's full text (arXiv PDF or a text version): the §2.3 and §2.4 constructions, the exact statement of the strong intersection conjecture, and the AI disclosure verbatim; the quotes here come from a fetch tool's extraction of the HTML, and the PDF text was not readable. (c) Huneke's independent verification note in the Pham repository, and whether the Pham example is in characteristic zero only. (d) Christensen–Gerko–Iyengar's ring: characteristic and embedding dimension of the counterexample, to reconcile with their equicharacteristic embedding-dimension-≤3 proof. (e) The OpenAI preprints: their arXiv or repository location and date; whether the Artin algebras are commutative (the Lean files AuslanderReiten.lean and Tachikawa.lean, or the preprint's quiver and relations); whether the Lean build is sorry-free; and the authors' own account of how the result was produced. (f) Dutta's 1987 paper and the SLMath notes, to settle which 'strong intersection conjecture' the equivalence with the canonical element conjecture refers to. (g) Dates: Pham's repository first commit; Lyle's posting date; the day of the OpenAI release. (h) Whether any expert has verified Ma's counterexamples beyond Christensen–Nasseh's citation, or whether any later paper contradicts them.

judgement.why: The statement names a family, so no single event can be whole; everything settling one named conjecture or a restricted class is a case. I read the family as the homological conjectures of commutative algebra: the article's fourteen items plus the commutative Peskine–Szpiro, Huneke–Şega–Vraciu, Huneke–Wiegand and commutative Auslander–Reiten conjectures, which belong to the same literature. Artin-algebra (noncommutative) results, the answered questions that fall short of the conjectures, and neighbouring conjectures are variant. Equivalence theorems and neighbour papers are none. Ma's dimension-inequality counterexample is credited by the author's own disclosure to ChatGPT, so generated. Codex is credited with the CGI construction and the proof, so generated. Böhmler–Marczinzik ('found with the assistance') and Pham ('assisted with the search') are assisted. Pham counts as digested because Huneke, named, independently recomputed the example, and CGI corroborate it. Böhmler–Marczinzik's 5-dimensional algebra is directly checkable. The OpenAI 193 Serre-positivity claim is a case (only the positivity half of item 13) and doubtful, because of the specific gaps the record names. OpenAI 195 refutes item 14 and is a case, unreviewed; its Lean check covers only the ring's properties.
judgement.doubts: Family scope is the main judgement call: if only the article's 14 named items count, then Ma, Böhmler–Marczinzik, Pham, CGI, Christensen–Nasseh and Lyle would be variant, and only KC–Soto Levins and OpenAI 193/195 would remain. Pham's repository is undated, but it was cited by 21 Aug 2026, so it falls after the snapshot either way. Huneke's verification note itself was not read. The CGI counterexample and proof have an unresolved consistency question. The Ma dimension counterexample is AI-found, but the grade counterexample is the author's own; I rated the bundled event by its strongest contribution.
